title: token-rotation-intermittent-authorization-briefing-for-customers-2027-09-23
content:
Executive summary:

On 2027-09-23 between 07:12 and 09:03 UTC, a subset of requests to Redwood Private control-plane endpoints experienced intermittent authorization failures (403/401). The failures affected customers using automatic key rotation with customer-managed KMS integration; impact was isolated to Private (VPC/on-prem packaged control-plane) deployments in two regions (eu-west-1 and us-east-1). We resolved the immediate availability issue at 09:03 UTC.

This doc is a customer-facing briefing and draft postmortem intended for partner communications and the public status page. It includes a short status update you can paste into your status page, a detailed timeline, root cause analysis, remediation steps we performed, ongoing mitigations, and suggested customer actions.

Status page short update (to paste):
Redwood Inference -- Resolved: 2027-09-23 09:03 UTC. Between 07:12 and 09:03 UTC we saw intermittent authorization failures for some Private deployments using customer-managed key rotation. The issue has been mitigated; affected customers may have seen request rejections or elevated error rates. We apologize for the disruption. A follow-up with technical details and next steps is being shared with affected partners.

Who should read this:
- Customers with Private deployments and KMS-integrated token rotation
- Platform and security teams managing tokens in their VPC/on-prem stacks
- Partner SRE contacts and CSMs handling impacted accounts

Impact summary:
- Scope: ~14 customers (mix of enterprise and mid-market) with automatic rotation enabled; not all customers in affected regions.
- Symptoms: 401/403 responses to inference API calls and control-plane requests during rotation windows, failures were intermittent (some requests succeeded).
- Duration: 1 hour 51 minutes total; full mitigation at 09:03 UTC.
- SLA: transient SLA breaches for affected requests; we are evaluating credits for customers whose available throughput was materially impacted.

Timeline (UTC):
- 07:09: Operator-run scheduled KMS rotation kick-off window begins for eu-west-1.
- 07:12: First customer alert received via monitoring: spike in 403s for a Private deployment. Automated alert routed to SRE and Customer Success on-call.
- 07:18: Engineering investigation: logs show token validation failures originating at control-plane edge nodes.
- 07:25: Observed pattern: failures occur when rotation orchestration and token-cache eviction overlap on leader-election boundary (rare race).
- 07:40: Temporary mitigation: disabled auto-rotation orchestration for the current rotation window in eu-west-1 and forced cache-warm for impacted control-plane nodes.
- 08:05: Similar failures detected in us-east-1 during a staggered rotation; mitigation steps applied there as well.
- 08:50: Deploy hotfix (runtime PR #1987) to edge token validator that makes rotation apply atomically and introduces short backoff/retry for validation while caches transition.
- 09:03: Hotfix roll-forward completed to all affected control-plane nodes; error rates return to baseline.

Root cause (summary):
During scheduled KMS-backed key rotations, the rotation coordinator performed three actions: rotate key metadata, evict token validation cache, and notify edge nodes. Under specific timing (leader transition + overlapping cache eviction), edge nodes processed requests using stale rotation metadata while cache eviction/invalidation was in-flight. The token validator's previous implementation performed a metadata read and cache eviction in non-atomic steps; in a narrow window this produced validation checks against unrecognized key identifiers, causing 401/403 responses for tokens that were still valid from the client perspective.

Contributing factors:
- New orchestration optimizer (deployed 2027-08) changed timing of meta updates to reduce rotation latency; altered timing exposed a race in validation logic.
- Limited telemetry for in-flight rotation states at edge nodes. Existing metrics showed error counts but not the underlying cache state transitions.

What we did (immediate):
1) Emergency mitigation: disabled scheduled automatic rotation for in-progress windows in the two regions to stop new rotation operations.
2) Cache warm and manual sync: performed cache warming and manual metadata sync on control-plane edge nodes for impacted clusters.
3) Hotfix roll-out: released PR #1987 with two changes: (a) make rotation metadata update and cache eviction atomic using a two-phase commit at the edge validator; (b) add a short retry/backoff path so transient validation mismatches are retried quickly (keeps tail latency low).
4) Monitoring: added a temporary log alert to detect any validation attempts during rotation windows and an elevated error-rate pager.

What we will do (longer-term fixes):
- Instrumentation: ship richer rotation-state metrics so we can tell when nodes are mid-rotation, including cache version tags and leader identity.
- Orchestration: update rotation coordinator to perform cross-region drain-and-apply steps for Private deployments with customer-managed KMS to avoid parallel rotations overlapping leader transitions.
- Testing: add multi-node rotation race tests to the CI harness and run periodic stress tests that exercise leader-election timings.
- Rollout policy: add a safety window and canary checks for any change to rotation timing or orchestration optimizers.

Customer-facing remediation and recommended actions:
- Immediate: No action required for most customers; tokens issued prior to the window remain valid. If you saw sustained failures, please contact Support with request traces (x-request-id headers) so we can map to impacted nodes.
- If you use automated rotation on your side in addition to Redwood-managed rotation, consider pausing non-essential rotations until our postmortem actions are completed.
- For customers who use HSM-backed rotation and pinned secrets: our recommended configuration is to enable "rotation-quorum" mode (we will follow up with a config guide) to avoid leader-bound rotation races.

Compensation / SLA considerations:
We are quantifying customer impact and will proactively reach out to accounts with measurable throughput loss to discuss SLA credits or other remediation. If you believe your application experienced material disruption (beyond transient retries), please open a ticket and escalate to your CSM.

Communication plan and customer outreach:
- Affected customers: CSMs will reach out with this briefing + request logs within 24 hours.
- Status page: brief update posted now; a follow-up public postmortem will be published to our status page and Confluence once engineering finishes the root cause write-up and fix verification (ETA 2027-09-30).
- Partners: we will notify channel partners and any marketplace listings where impacted customers may be referenced.

Questions we expect and suggested responses for CSMs:
Q: Should I rotate my keys now?
A: No — rotating keys during our ongoing changes risks re-triggering edge metadata mismatches. Wait for guidance from your CSM; we will publish a safe timeline.

Q: How likely is this to recur?
A: We have applied a hotfix to make metadata application atomic and added temporary monitoring. The underlying race is now covered by the hotfix and we will add stronger instrumentation and testing. Residual risk is low but we will confirm with canary rotations over the next week.

Q: What if my app saw data loss or incorrect responses?
A: This incident caused authorization failures (rejections), not content corruption. No inference data should have been lost. If you see behavior that suggests otherwise, escalate immediately.

Technical appendix (for engineering-savvy customers):
- Root files/links: JIRA ENG-5421 (rotation race), PR runtime#1987 (atomic-rotation-apply), Confluence incident page https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INC/INC-2027-09-23-token-rotation.
- Code change summary: token_validator.go: make ApplyRotationMetadata atomic by acquiring in-memory rotation-version lock and publishing new metadata under version tag; add ValidateWithFallback that checks current cache, then performs a metadata fetch and retry if validation fails. Add metrics: rotation.cache_version, rotation.in_flight_count.

Support contacts and next steps:
- Primary contact: Maya Chen (CSM) — maya.chen@redwood.ai — will coordinate outreach for affected accounts.
- Engineering lead: David Ruiz (Eng) — david.ruiz@redwood.ai — for technical deep dives.
- For urgent escalations, open a Priority ticket via the portal and add the tag "inc-2027-09-23-token-rotation".

Draft notes for public postmortem (to be expanded):
- One-line summary, timeline, root cause, fixes applied, verification steps, long-term mitigations, and apology.
- Verify instrumentation and canary schedule before publishing.

Internal follow-up actions (owner assignments):
- ENG: Add race tests to CI (owner: Liam O'Connor, due 2027-10-07).
- Infra: Add rotation-state metrics and dashboards (owner: Priya Nair, due 2027-10-01).
- CS: Contact impacted customers and collect traces (owner: Maya Chen, complete by 2027-09-24).

Draft status-page copy (short):
We experienced intermittent authorization failures affecting some Private deployments using customer-managed KMS during scheduled key rotations between 07:12 and 09:03 UTC on 2027-09-23. The issue has been mitigated; we are following up with impacted customers and will publish a full postmortem.

Apology: We apologize for the disruption. Ensuring stable, predictable inference for Private deployments is a top priority and we recognize the impact this had on affected customers.

-- End of customer brief draft --

Notes to self: keep this version lean — we will expand the technical appendix and attach logs once ENG completes the verification run.
